units.zh: 盧文紀，字子持，京兆萬年人。
units.en: Lu Wenji, courtesy name Zichi, came from Wannian in the Jingzhao commandery.
units.literal: Lu Wenji, styled Zichi, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 〈（案：此下原有闕文。）〉
units.en: Note: The original text below was missing.
units.literal: Note: The original text below was missing.

units.zh: 長興末，為太常卿。
units.en: Late in the Changxing reign he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he served as Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 文紀形貌魁偉，語音高朗，占對鏗鏘，健於飲啖。
units.en: Wenji was tall and imposing, spoke in a clear, carrying voice, answered audiences with ringing assurance, and ate and drank with hearty appetite.
units.literal: Wenji had a tall, imposing physique, a high, clear voice, and a resonant manner in audience; he was hearty in eating and drinking.

units.zh: 奉使蜀川，路由岐下，時唐末帝為岐帥，以主禮待之，觀其儀形旨趣，遇之頗厚。
units.en: While on embassy to Shu he traveled through Qi, where the future Last Emperor of Tang held the Qi governorship and received him with a host's courtesy. Struck by Wenji's bearing and manner, he showed him exceptional regard.
units.literal: On a mission to Shu he passed through Qi; at that time the Last Emperor of Tang was military governor of Qi and received him with the courtesy due a sovereign guest. Observing his bearing and intent, the governor treated him with marked favor.

units.zh: 清泰初，中書闕輔相，末帝訪之於朝，左右曰：「臣見班行中所譽，當大拜者，姚顗、盧文紀、崔居儉耳。」
units.en: Early in Qingtai, with no vice-chancellor in the Secretariat, the Last Emperor asked the court whom to appoint. Attendants said, "Of those the ranks most commend for great promotion, I see Yao Hao, Lu Wenji, and Cui Jujian."
units.literal: Early in the Qingtai era the Secretariat lacked a chief counselor; the Last Emperor inquired of the court, and those at his side said, "Among those praised in the ranks whom Your Majesty should promote to high office, I see Yao Hao, Lu Wenji, and Cui Jujian."

units.zh: 或品藻三人才行，其心愈惑。
units.en: When others weighed the three men's character and ability, he grew only more uncertain.
units.literal: When some appraised the three men's conduct and talent, his mind grew all the more unsettled.

units.zh: 末帝乃俱書當時清望達官數人姓名，投琉璃瓶中，月夜焚香，禱請於天，旭旦以箸挾之，首得文紀之名，次即姚顗。
units.en: The emperor wrote the names of several leading officials of the day, dropped them into a glass jar, burned incense under the moon, and prayed to Heaven. At dawn he drew with chopsticks: Wenji's name came first, then Yao Hao's.
units.literal: The Last Emperor then wrote together the names of several eminent officials of the day, placed them in a glass jar, burned incense by moonlight, and prayed to Heaven; at dawn he drew lots with chopsticks—the first name drawn was Wenji's, the next Yao Hao's.

units.zh: 末帝素已奇待，歡然命之，即授中書侍郎、同平章事，與姚顗同升相位。
units.en: He had long held Wenji in special regard. Pleased, he appointed him Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, elevating him to chief minister alongside Yao Hao.
units.literal: The Last Emperor had long regarded him as extraordinary; delighted, he appointed him—at once Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat-Chancellery, rising to the chief ministership together with Yao Hao.

units.zh: 時朝廷兵革之後，宗社甫寧，外寇內侵，強臣在境。
units.en: The court had only just settled the realm after years of war; enemies threatened from without and powerful generals held the frontiers.
units.literal: At that time, after years of warfare, the altars had only just been secured; foreign enemies pressed inward and powerful subjects held the borders.

units.zh: 文紀處經綸之地，無輔弼之謀，所論者愛憎朋黨之小瑕，所糾者銓選擬掄之微颣。
units.en: Though he occupied the seat of statecraft, Wenji offered no true ministerial counsel. He busied himself with petty factional grudges and trifling flaws in appointments and promotions.
units.literal: Wenji stood in the place of statecraft yet offered no counsel fit for a helper; what he discussed were petty blemishes of factional love and hate, and what he impeached were slight faults in selection and appointment.

units.zh: 時有蜀人史在德為太常丞，出入權要之門，評品朝士，多有譏彈，乃上章云：「文武兩班，宜選能進用。
units.en: A Shu native, Shi Zaide, served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He haunted the powerful, judged courtiers, and often mocked them. He memorialized: "Both civil and military ranks should be filled by selecting the capable.
units.literal: At the time a man of Shu named Shi Zaide was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he frequented the doors of the powerful, appraised court officials, and often cast ridicule. He submitted a memorial saying, "Both civil and military cohorts should be chosen and advanced on merit.

units.zh: 見在軍都將校、朝廷士大夫，並請閱試澄汰，能者進用，否者黜退，不限名位高下。」
units.en: All active army commanders and court grandees should be tested and winnowed: the able promoted, the unfit removed, with no regard to rank."
units.literal: All serving army commanders and court grandees should be examined and sifted—the able promoted, the unfit dismissed, without limit of rank high or low."

units.zh: 疏下中書，文紀以為非己，怒甚，召諫議大夫盧損為覆狀，辭旨蕪漫，為眾所嗤。
units.en: When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Wenji took it as a personal attack and was furious. He had Remonstrance Officer Lu Sun draft a reply; the prose was vague and rambling, and everyone laughed at it.
units.literal: When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Wenji took it as directed against himself and was furious. He summoned Remonstrance Officer Lu Sun to draft a rebuttal; the wording was muddled and diffuse, and the crowd mocked it.

units.zh: 三年夏，晉祖引契丹拒命，既而大軍挫衄，官寨受圍。
units.en: That summer in the third year, the Jin founder brought in Khitan forces in rebellion. The main army was soon broken and the imperial encampment surrounded.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year the Jin Ancestor led the Khitans in defiance; soon the great army suffered defeat and the imperial camp was besieged.

units.zh: 八月，親征，過徽陵，拜於闕下，休於仗舍。
units.en: In the eighth month he took the field in person. At Huiling he bowed beneath the gate-tower and rested in the guard-house.
units.literal: In the eighth month the emperor led the campaign in person; passing Huiling he bowed below the gate-tower and rested in the guard-house.

units.zh: 文紀扈從，帝顧謂之曰：「朕聞主憂臣辱，予自鳳翔來，首命卿為宰相，聽人所論，將為便致太平，今寇孽紛紛，令萬乘自行戰賊，於汝安乎？」
units.en: Wenji followed the campaign. The emperor turned to him and said, "They say the minister shares the ruler's shame. Since Fengxiang I made you chancellor first, believing men who said you would soon restore peace. Now rebels swarm and I must ride out to fight them myself—does that sit well with you?"
units.literal: Wenji attended him; the emperor turned and said to him, "I have heard that when the ruler grieves, the minister is shamed. Since I came from Fengxiang I first named you chancellor, trusting men's talk that you would soon bring peace. Now rebels swarm and I must lead the imperial carriage to fight bandits myself—are you at ease with this?"

units.zh: 文紀惶恐致謝。
units.en: Wenji thanked him in terror.
units.literal: Wenji thanked him in fear and trembling.

units.zh: 時末帝季年，天奪其魄，聲言救寨，其實倦行。
units.en: The Last Emperor was in his final years; Heaven had dimmed his vigor. He spoke of relieving the camp, but in truth he had grown weary of campaigning.
units.literal: At that time the Last Emperor was in his declining years; Heaven had taken his spirit. He proclaimed rescue of the camp, but in truth he wearied of the march.

units.zh: 初次河陽，召文紀、張延朗謀議。
units.en: When he first reached Heyang he called Wenji and Zhang Yanlang to deliberate.
units.literal: On first reaching Heyang he summoned Wenji and Zhang Yanlang for counsel.

units.zh: 文紀曰：「敵騎倏往忽來，無利則去，大寨牢固，足以枝梧，況已有三處救兵，可以不戰而解。
units.en: Wenji said, "Enemy cavalry strike and vanish; they withdraw when there is no profit. The main camp is strong enough to hold, and three relief forces are already moving. The siege can be raised without fighting.
units.literal: Wenji said, "The enemy's horsemen come and go in a flash; when there is no gain they leave. The great camp is solid and can be braced against them; moreover three relief armies are already in place, so the siege may be lifted without battle.

units.zh: 使人督促，責以成功，輿駕且駐河橋，詳觀事勢，況地處舟車之要，正當天下之心，必若未能解圍，去亦非晚。」
units.en: Dispatch envoys to press them for results. Let the imperial train pause at Heqiao and observe events. The spot commands river and road traffic and the empire's attention. If relief fails, withdrawal will still be in time."
units.literal: Send men to urge them and hold them to success; let the imperial carriage halt at Heqiao and watch how matters unfold. Moreover this place commands river and road traffic and holds the heart of the realm. If the siege cannot be raised, withdrawal will not be too late."

units.zh: 會延朗與趙延壽款密，傍奏曰：「文紀之言是也。」
units.en: Yanlang was then intimate with Zhao Yanshou. He whispered: "Wenji is right."
units.literal: At that juncture Yanlang was on intimate terms with Zhao Yanshou; he spoke aside and said, "Wenji's words are right."

units.zh: 故令延壽北行，末帝坐俟其敗。
units.en: So Yanshou was sent north while the Last Emperor sat back expecting his failure.
units.literal: So Yanshou was sent north, and the Last Emperor sat waiting for his defeat.

units.zh: 晉祖入洛，罷相為吏部尚書，再遷太子少傅。
units.en: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, Wenji left the chief ministership for director of the Ministry of Personnel, then was promoted again to junior tutor of the heir.
units.literal: When the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, Wenji was removed from the chief ministership and made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted again to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，改太子太傅。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made grand tutor of the heir.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, he was changed to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 漢祖登極，轉太子太師。
units.en: When the Han founder took the throne, he became grand mentor of the heir.
units.literal: When the Han founder ascended the throne, he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 時朝官分司在洛，雖有留臺御史，紀綱亦多不整肅，遂敕文紀別令檢轄。
units.en: Court officials then held branch offices in Luoyang. Though leave-behind censors existed, discipline was often lax, so Wenji was ordered to serve separately as special inspector.
units.literal: At that time court officials with branch offices in Luoyang had leave-behind censors, yet discipline was often not strict; Wenji was therefore ordered to serve separately as special inspector.

units.zh: 侍御史趙礪及糾分司朝臣中有行香拜表疏怠者，楊邠怒，凡疾病不在朝謁者，皆與致仕官。
units.en: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.
units.literal: Attending Censor Zhao Li and others impeached Luoyang branch officials lax in incense rites and memorial audiences. Yang Bin grew angry and granted retirement to all who claimed illness and stayed away from court audiences.

units.zh: 時文紀別令檢轄之職，頗甚滋章，因疾請假，復為留臺所奏，遂以本官致仕。
units.en: Wenji's special inspection duties grew increasingly burdensome. After he took sick leave, the leave-behind office impeached him again, and he retired at his original rank.
units.literal: At the time Wenji's duties as special inspector grew increasingly burdensome. Taking sick leave, he was again impeached by the leave-behind office and retired at his original rank.

units.zh: （《歐陽史》：周太祖入立，即拜司空於家。）
units.en: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)
units.literal: (The History of Ouyang: When Zhou Taizu took power, Wenji was at once appointed Grand Master of Works at home.)

units.zh: 廣順元年夏卒，年七十六。
units.en: He died in summer of the first year of Guangshun, aged seventy-six.
units.literal: He died in summer of the first year of Guangshun, aged seventy-six.

units.zh: 贈司徒，輟視朝一日。
units.en: He was posthumously made minister over the masses and court audience was suspended one day.
units.literal: Posthumously made Minister over the Masses; court audience was suspended one day.

units.zh: 文紀平生積財巨萬，及卒，為其子龜齡所費，不數年間，以至蕩盡，由是多藏者以為誡焉。
units.en: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life, but after his death his son Guiling spent it within a few years until nothing remained, and many hoarders thereafter took this as a warning.
units.literal: Wenji had amassed great wealth in life; after his death his son Guiling spent it all within a few years until nothing remained—whereafter many hoarders took this as a warning.

units.zh: 馬裔孫，字慶先，棣州商河人。
units.en: Ma Yisun, courtesy name Qingxian, was from Shanghe in Dizhou.
units.literal: Ma Yisun, styled Qingxian, was a native of Shanghe in Dizhou.

units.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。）〉
units.en: Note: Text is missing below.
units.literal: Note: Text is missing below.

units.zh: 唐末帝即位，用為翰林學士、戶部郎中、知制誥，賜金紫，未滿歲，改中書舍人、禮部侍郎，皆帶禁職。
units.en: When the Last Emperor of Tang acceded, Yisun became Hanlin academician, revenue bureau director, and drafting officer for edicts, with gold-purple insignia. Within the year he was made secretariat drafter and vice minister of rites, retaining palace duties.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang took the throne, Yisun was made Hanlin Academician, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Drafting Officer for Imperial Edicts, with the gold-purple distinction. Before a year had passed he was changed to Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites, all with forbidden-office duties.

units.zh: 尋拜中書侍郎、平章事。
units.en: He was soon made vice minister of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 裔孫純儒，性多凝滯，遽登相位，未悉朝廷舊事。
units.en: A bookish man, slow and obstructive by temperament, he was suddenly elevated to chief minister without mastering the court's old ways.
units.literal: Yisun was a pure scholar, slow and obstructive by nature; suddenly raised to the chief ministership, he did not yet know the court's old practices.

units.zh: 初，馮道罷同州入朝，拜司空。
units.en: Earlier Feng Dao had left Tongzhou for court and been appointed Grand Master of Works.
units.literal: Earlier, Feng Dao left Tongzhou and entered court, receiving appointment as Grand Master of Works.

units.zh: 唐朝故事，三公為加官，無單拜者，是時朝議率爾命道，制出，或曰「三公正宰相，便合參大政」；
units.en: Tang precedent treated the Three Excellencies as honorary posts without separate audiences. The court now appointed Dao offhand. When the order appeared, some said, "The three excellencies are true chancellors and should join great affairs at once";
units.literal: By Tang precedent the Three Excellencies were supernumerary titles, with no separate audience; at that time the court's deliberation casually ordered Dao. When the edict issued, some said, "The Three Excellencies are true chancellors and ought at once to take part in great affairs";

units.zh: 又云「合受冊」。
units.en: others that "he should receive formal investiture."
units.literal: others said he "ought to receive investiture."

units.zh: 眾言藉藉。
units.en: Rumor swirled through the court.
units.literal: Talk buzzed everywhere.

units.zh: 盧文紀又欲祭祀時便令掃除，馮道聞之曰：「司空掃除，職也，吾無所憚。」
units.en: Lu Wenji also wanted Feng Dao to sweep the halls during sacrifices. Feng Dao heard and said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty; I do not shrink from it."
units.literal: Lu Wenji also wished to have sweeping done at the time of sacrifices; when Feng Dao heard it he said, "Sweeping is the Grand Master of Works' duty—I have no fear of it."

units.zh: 既而知非乃止。
units.en: When he saw the proposal was wrong, he dropped it.
units.literal: Once he knew it was wrong he stopped.

units.zh: 劉句為僕射，性剛，群情嫉之，乃共贊右常侍孔昭序論行香次第，言：「常侍侍從之臣，行立合在僕射之前。」
units.en: Liu Gou served as left vice director; his stiffness bred resentment. Courtiers backed Right Regular Attendant Kong Zhaoxu's memorial on incense order, arguing that "a regular attendant attends the sovereign and should walk before a vice director."
units.literal: Liu Gou was Left Vice Director; stiff by nature, the crowd resented him. They jointly praised Right Regular Attendant Kong Zhaoxu for a memorial on the order of offering incense, saying, "The regular attendant is a attendant of the ruler and ought to walk and stand before the vice director."

units.zh: 疏奏，下御史臺定例。
units.en: The memorial went to the Censorate to fix precedent.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted it went down to the Censorate to fix precedent.

units.zh: 同光已來，李琪、盧質繼為僕射，質性輕脫，不能守師長之體，故昭序輕言。
units.en: Since Tongguang, Li Qi and Lu Zhi had held the post; Zhi was flighty and failed the senior's demeanor, which emboldened Zhaoxu.
units.literal: Since Tongguang, Li Qi and Lu Zhi had in turn been vice directors; Zhi was light and unbridled and could not keep the demeanor of a senior, so Zhaoxu spoke lightly.

units.zh: 裔孫以群情不悅劉句、馮道，欲微抑之，乃責臺司，須檢則例，而臺吏言：「舊不見例，據南北班位，即常侍在前。」
units.en: Because the court disliked Liu Gou and Feng Dao, Yisun wished to humble them slightly. He rebuked the Censorate to find precedent; clerks replied, "No old case exists; by north-south court order the regular attendant precedes."
units.literal: Yisun, because the crowd disliked Liu Gou and Feng Dao, wished to check them slightly; he therefore reproved the Censorate, demanding search of precedent, but the clerks said, "No old precedent is found; by north-south court order the regular attendant stands before."

units.zh: 俄屬國忌，將就列未定，裔孫即判臺狀曰：「既有援據，足可遵行，各示本官。」
units.en: When a national mourning observance came and ranks were not yet set, Yisun ruled on the censorial report: "With supporting authority, this may be followed—each official to his station."
units.literal: Soon it was a national mourning day; as the ranks were about to form but not yet settled, Yisun at once ruled on the Censorate report: "Since there is supporting authority, it may fully be followed—show each official his place."

units.zh: 劉句怒，揮袂而退。
units.en: Liu Gou flung his sleeve and left in anger.
units.literal: Liu Gou in anger swept his sleeve and withdrew.

units.zh: 自後日責臺司定例，崔居儉謂南宮同列曰：「從昭序言語，是朝廷人總不解語也。
units.en: Afterward he daily demanded the Censorate fix precedent. Cui Jujian told Southern Palace colleagues, "To follow Zhaoxu's words is to say the whole court cannot speak properly.
units.literal: Thereafter he daily pressed the Censorate to fix precedent. Cui Jujian said to colleagues in the Southern Palace, "Following Zhaoxu's words—court men altogether fail to understand speech.

units.zh: 且僕射師長也，中丞大夫就班修敬，常侍班在南宮六卿之下，況僕射乎。
units.en: A vice director is a senior. Censors and grandees take station and show respect; a regular attendant ranks below the Southern Palace's six ministers—how much more below a vice director?
units.literal: Moreover the vice director is a teacher; censors and grandees take their places and show respect—the regular attendant's rank stands below the Six Ministers of the Southern Palace, how much more below a vice director?

units.zh: 已前騎省年深，望南宮二侍郎如仰霄漢，癡人舉止，何取笑之深耶！」
units.en: Veterans of the Mounted Guard once looked up to the two vice ministers as to the Milky Way. What foolishness, and how deep the mockery!"
units.literal: In former years the Mounted Guard was long in service; gazing at the Southern Palace's two vice ministers was like looking up at the Milky Way—what folly, and how deep the ridicule!"

units.zh: 眾聞居儉言，紛議稍息。
units.en: Hearing Jujian, the uproar slowly died down.
units.literal: When the crowd heard Jujian's words, the clamor gradually subsided.

units.zh: 文士哂裔孫堂判有「援據」二字，其中書百職，裔孫素未諳練，無能專決，但署名而已。
units.en: Writers mocked Yisun's ruling for the phrase "supporting authority." Of the Secretariat's hundred duties he was unpracticed and decided nothing—only signed.
units.literal: Literati mocked Yisun's desk ruling for the words "supporting authority"; of the Secretariat's hundred duties Yisun had never been practiced and could decide nothing—he only signed his name.

units.zh: 又少見賓客，時人目之為「三不開」，謂口不開、印不開、門不開也。
units.en: He rarely received guests. People called him the "Three Unopened": mouth, seal, and door.
units.literal: He also rarely received guests; men of the time called him the "Three Unopened"—mouth unopened, seal unopened, door unopened.

units.zh: 及太原事起，唐末帝幸懷州，裔孫留司在洛。
units.en: When trouble broke at Taiyuan the Last Emperor went to Huai Prefecture; Yisun stayed in Luoyang as capital chief.
units.literal: When the Taiyuan affair arose the Last Emperor of Tang went to Huai Prefecture; Yisun remained in Luoyang as chief of the capital office.

units.zh: 未幾，趙德鈞父子有異志，官寨危急，君臣計無所出。
units.en: Soon Zhao Dejun and his son showed disloyal intent. The camp was desperate and court and emperor found no plan.
units.literal: Before long Zhao Dejun and his son harbored disloyal intent; the imperial camp was critical and ruler and ministers had no plan.

units.zh: 俄而裔孫自洛來朝，眾相謂曰：「馬相此來，必有安危之策。」
units.en: Suddenly Yisun came from Luoyang to court. All said, "Chancellor Ma must bring a policy for survival."
units.literal: Suddenly Yisun came from Luoyang to audience; all said to one another, "Chancellor Ma's coming must mean a policy for safety or peril."

units.zh: 既至，獻綾三百匹，卒無獻可之言。
units.en: He presented three hundred bolts of silk—and no counsel worth taking.
units.literal: When he arrived he presented three hundred bolts of silk and in the end offered no counsel worth adopting.

units.zh: 晉祖受命，廢歸田里。
units.en: When the Jin founder took the Mandate, Yisun was sent home.
units.literal: When the Jin Ancestor received the Mandate, Yisun was dismissed to his home district.

units.zh: 裔孫好名，慕韓愈之為人，尤不重佛。
units.en: Yisun loved fame, admired Han Yu, and especially despised Buddhism.
units.literal: Yisun loved reputation and admired Han Yu's example, especially disdaining Buddhism.

units.zh: 及廢居裏巷，追感唐末帝平昔之遇，乃依長壽僧舍讀佛書，冀申冥報。
units.en: Dismissed to the lanes, he remembered the Last Emperor's kindness and read Buddhist texts at Longevity Monastery, hoping to repay him beyond the grave.
units.literal: After dismissal he lived in lanes and alleys; recalling the Last Emperor's former kindness, he lodged at the Longevity Monastery to read Buddhist books, hoping to repay him in the unseen world.

units.zh: 歲餘枕藉黃卷中，見《華嚴》、《楞嚴》，詞理富贍，由是酷賞之，仍抄撮之，相形於歌詠，謂之《法喜集》；
units.en: A year among sutras brought him to the Avatamsaka and Surangama, rich in doctrine. He admired them, copied passages, and wove them into verse as Joy in the Dharma;
units.literal: For more than a year, buried among yellow scrolls, he saw the Avatamsaka and Surangama Sutras, rich in doctrine and reason; he therefore admired them deeply, copied selections, and set them beside his songs, calling the collection Joy in the Dharma;

units.zh: 又纂諸經要言為《佛國記》，凡數千言。
units.en: and compiled essential passages as Record of the Buddha Land, several thousand words.
units.literal: he also compiled essential passages of the scriptures as Record of the Buddha Land, several thousand words in all.

units.zh: 或嘲之曰：「公生平以傅奕、韓愈為高識，何前倨而後恭，是佛佞公耶？
units.en: Some teased him: "You held Fu Yi and Han Yu as models—why proud before and humble after? Is the Buddha fawning on you?
units.literal: Some mocked him: "In life you took Fu Yi and Han Yu as your models of insight—why so proud before and so deferential after? Is the Buddha fawning on you?

units.zh: 公佞佛耶？」
units.en: Or are you fawning on the Buddha?"
units.literal: Or are you fawning on the Buddha?"

units.zh: 裔孫笑而答曰：「佛佞予則多矣。」
units.en: Yisun smiled: "If the Buddha fawns on me, it has done so plenty."
units.literal: Yisun answered with a smile, "If the Buddha fawns on me, it has done so often enough."

units.zh: 李崧相晉，用李專美為贊善，裔孫以賓客致仕，專美轉少卿，裔孫得太子詹事。
units.en: When Li Song served Jin, he made Li Zhuanmei aide to the heir; Yisun retired as guest, Zhuanmei rose to vice director, and Yisun became grand mentor of the heir.
units.literal: When Li Song was chancellor of Jin he used Li Zhuanmei as aide; Yisun retired as a guest, Zhuanmei became vice director, and Yisun received Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 晉、漢公卿以裔孫好為文章，皆欣然待之。
units.en: Grandees of Jin and Han, knowing his love of letters, welcomed him gladly.
units.literal: Jin and Han grandees, because Yisun loved to write, all received him gladly.

units.zh: 太祖即位，就加檢校禮部尚書、太子賓客，分司在洛。
units.en: When Taizu acceded he was made inspector-general of rites and guest of the heir, with duty at Luoyang.
units.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he was further made Inspector-General of the Ministry of Rites and Guest of the Heir Apparent, with office at Luoyang.

units.zh: 每閉關養素，惟事謳吟著述。
units.en: He shut his doors, lived simply, and devoted himself to verse and books.
units.literal: He shut his doors to nurture simplicity and devoted himself only to chanting and writing.

units.zh: 嗜八分書，題尺酬答，必親劄以炫其墨跡。
units.en: He loved clerical script and always wrote titles and replies himself to show his brush.
units.literal: He loved clerical script; for titles and replies on letters he always wrote in his own hand to display his brushwork.

units.zh: 裔孫將卒之前，睹白虺緣於庭槐，驅之失所在，裔孫感賦鵬之文，作《槐蟲賦》以見誌。
units.en: Before his death he saw a white serpent on the courtyard locust; driven off, it vanished. He wrote on the roc and composed Record of the Locust Worm to record his mood.
units.literal: Before Yisun was to die he saw a white serpent on the courtyard locust; when driven off it vanished. Moved, he wrote an essay on the roc and composed Record of the Locust Worm to express his mind.

units.zh: 廣順三年秋七月，卒於洛陽。
units.en: In the seventh month of autumn, Guangshun year three, he died in Luoyang.
units.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the third year of Guangshun he died in Luoyang.

units.zh: 詔贈太子少傅，輟視朝一日。
units.en: The throne posthumously made him junior tutor of the heir and suspended audience one day.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and suspended court audience for one day.

units.zh: 裔孫初為河中從事，因事赴闕，宿於邏店。
units.en: He had first served as aide in Hezhong; on business he reached the capital and lodged at a relay station.
units.literal: Yisun had first been an aide in Hezhong; on business he went to the capital and lodged at a relay station.

units.zh: 其地有上邏神祠，夜夢神見召，待以優禮，手授二筆，其筆一大一小，覺而異焉。
units.en: A shrine to the Spirit of Shangluo stood there. He dreamed the spirit summoned him, honored him, and placed two brushes in his hand, one large, one small; waking, he marveled.
units.literal: The place had a shrine to the Spirit of Shangluo; at night he dreamed the spirit summoned him, treated him with honored courtesy, and placed in his hand two brushes, one large and one small; on waking he marveled.

units.zh: 及為翰林學士，裔孫以為契鴻筆之兆。
units.en: As Hanlin academician he took this as an omen of the covenant brush.
units.literal: When he became Hanlin Academician Yisun took this as an omen of the writing brush of the covenant.

units.zh: 旋知貢舉，私自謂曰：「此二筆之應也。」
units.en: Soon he oversaw examinations and said privately, "Here is the two-brush omen."
units.literal: Soon he oversaw the examinations and said privately, "This is the fulfillment of the two brushes."

units.zh: 洎入中書上事，堂吏奉二筆，熟視大小如昔時夢中所授者。
units.en: Entering the Secretariat, desk clerks presented two brushes; their sizes matched the dream.
units.literal: When he entered the Secretariat to conduct affairs the desk clerks presented two brushes; looking closely, their sizes matched those given in the dream.

units.zh: 及卒後旬日，有侍婢靈語，一如裔孫聲氣，處分家事，皆有倫理，時人奇之。
units.en: Ten days after his death a maid spoke in his very voice, ordering the household with sound judgment; people were astonished.
units.literal: Some ten days after his death a serving maid spoke with a spirit voice just like Yisun's, ordering household affairs with full reason; men of the time thought it strange.

units.zh: 和凝，字成績，汶陽須昌人也。
units.en: He Ning, courtesy name Chengzhi, was from Xuchang in Wenyang.
units.literal: He Ning, styled Chengzhi, was a native of Xuchang in Wenyang.

units.zh: 九代祖逢堯，唐高宗時為監察御史，自逢堯之下，仕皆不顯。
units.en: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao had been a surveillance censor under Tang Gaozong; thereafter the line held no prominent office.
units.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao was a surveillance censor under Emperor Gaozong of Tang; from Fengyao down, office had not been prominent.

units.zh: 曾祖敞、祖濡皆以凝貴，累贈太師。
units.en: Great-grandfather Chang and grandfather Ru, through Ning's eminence, were repeatedly enfeoffed grand preceptor.
units.literal: Great-grandfather Chang and grandfather Ru, because of Ning's eminence, were repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 父矩，贈尚書令。
units.en: His father Ju was posthumously made grand mentor of the state.
units.literal: Father Ju was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the State.

units.zh: 矩性嗜酒，不拘禮節，雖素不知書，見士未嘗有慢色，必罄家財以延接。
units.en: Ju loved wine and ignored ritual. Though unlettered, he never slighted scholars and spent the family fortune to host them.
units.literal: Ju loved wine by nature and did not keep to ritual; though he knew no books by study, he never showed disrespect to scholars and would exhaust the family wealth to entertain them.

units.zh: 凝幼而聰敏，姿狀秀拔，神采射人。
units.en: Ning was clever as a boy, handsome and striking, with a gaze that arrested men.
units.literal: Ning was clever from childhood, with a handsome, outstanding bearing and a gaze that struck men.

units.zh: 少好學，書一覽者咸達其大義。
units.en: He loved learning; one reading of any book gave him its main sense.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning; whatever book he read once he grasped its main meaning.

units.zh: 年十七舉明經，至京師，忽夢人以五色筆一束以與之，謂曰：「子有如此才，何不舉進士？」
units.en: At seventeen he passed the Mingjing. In the capital he dreamed a man gave him five-colored brushes, saying, "With such talent, why not sit for the Jinshi?"
units.literal: At seventeen he passed the Mingjing examination; reaching the capital he suddenly dreamed a man gave him a bundle of brushes in five colors, saying, "With talent such as yours, why not take the Jinshi examination?"

units.zh: 自是才思敏贍，十九登進士第。
units.en: From then his wit grew quick and rich; at nineteen he passed the Jinshi.
units.literal: From then his literary thought grew nimble and rich; at nineteen he passed the Jinshi.

units.zh: 滑帥賀瑰知其名，辟置幕下。
units.en: He Gui, military governor of Hua, knew his name and took him on staff.
units.literal: Military Governor He Gui of Hua knew his name and recruited him to his staff.

units.zh: 凝善射。
units.en: Ning excelled at archery.
units.literal: Ning was skilled at archery.

units.zh: 時瑰與唐莊宗相拒於河上，戰胡柳陂，瑰軍敗而北，惟凝隨之，瑰顧曰：「子勿相隨，當自努力。」
units.en: Gui then opposed Zhuangzong on the Yellow River at Huliu Slope. Defeated, Gui fled north; only Ning followed. Gui said, "Do not follow—save yourself."
units.literal: At that time Gui opposed Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River; they fought at Huliu Slope. Gui's army was defeated and fled north; only Ning followed. Gui looked back and said, "Do not follow me—strive on your own."

units.zh: 凝泣而對曰：「丈夫受人知，有難不報，非素誌也，但恨未有死所。」
units.en: Ning wept: "A man who accepts trust and will not repay it in hardship was never my way; I only regret having no place to die."
units.literal: Ning wept and replied, "A man who has received another's trust and does not repay him in hardship—that was never my resolve; I only regret having no place to die."

units.zh: 旋有一騎士來逐瑰，凝叱之，不止，遂引弓以射，應弦而斃，瑰獲免。
units.en: A rider pursued Gui. Ning shouted; when the man did not stop, he shot and dropped him at the bowstring's sound; Gui was saved.
units.literal: Soon a rider came in pursuit of Gui; Ning shouted at him but he did not stop, so he drew the bow and shot; the man fell at the twang of the string and Gui was saved.

units.zh: 既而謂諸子曰：「昨非和公，無以至此。
units.en: He told his sons, "Without Lord He yesterday we would not be here.
units.literal: Afterward he told his sons, "Had it not been for Lord He yesterday, we would not be here.

units.zh: 和公文武全才而有志氣，後必享重位，爾宜謹事之。」
units.en: Lord He has civil and military talent and great resolve; he will surely reach high rank—serve him carefully."
units.literal: Lord He has full talent in civil and military affairs and great resolve; later he will surely enjoy high rank—you should serve him carefully."

units.zh: 遂以女妻之，由是聲望益隆。
units.en: He gave him his daughter, and Ning's renown grew.
units.literal: He then gave him his daughter in marriage, and from this his renown grew the more.

units.zh: 後歷鄆、鄧、洋三府從事。
units.en: He later served Yan, Deng, and Yang as aide.
units.literal: Later he served as aide in Yan, Deng, and Yang prefectures.

units.zh: 唐天成中，入拜殿中侍御史，歷禮部、刑部員外郎，改主客員外郎、知制誥，尋詔入翰林充學士，轉主客郎中充職，兼權知貢舉。
units.en: In Tang Tiancheng he became palace censor, then vice minister in rites and punishments, then guest vice director with drafting duties. Soon he entered the Hanlin as academician, became guest bureau director, and oversaw examinations.
units.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang he entered court as Palace Censor, passed through vice ministerships in Rites and Punishments, was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Guests with drafting duties, and soon was ordered into the Hanlin as academician; he became Bureau Director in Guests while keeping the post, and concurrently oversaw the examinations.

units.zh: 貢院舊例，放榜之日，設棘於門及閉院門，以防下第不逞者。
units.en: By examination-yard custom, on posting day thorns barred the gates and the yard closed against failed candidates.
units.literal: By old custom of the examination yard, on the day lists were posted thorn barriers were set at the gates and the yard gates closed, lest failed candidates make trouble.

units.zh: 凝令徹棘啟門，是日寂無喧者，所收多才名之士，時議以為得人。
units.en: Ning had the thorns removed and gates opened; that day was quiet. Most admitted were men of talent and name; opinion said he had chosen well.
units.literal: Ning ordered the thorns removed and the gates opened; that day there was no disturbance. Those admitted were mostly men of talent and name; opinion held that he had gained the right men.

units.zh: 〈（《澠水燕談》：範質初舉進士，時和凝知貢舉，凝嘗以宰輔自期，登第之日，名第十三人，及覽質文，尤加賞嘆，即以第十三名處之，場屋間謂之「傳衣缽」，若禪宗之相付授也。
units.en: 〈From Talks and Tales of the Mian Waters〉: When Fan Zhi first sat for the Jinshi, He Ning oversaw the examinations. Ning had long expected the chief ministership; on the day he passed, his own name was thirteenth. Reading Zhi's essay he admired it still more and placed him thirteenth. In the hall they called this "passing the robe and bowl," as in Chan succession.
units.literal: 〈The Waters of Mian: Talks and Tales〉: When Fan Zhi first took the Jinshi, He Ning was overseeing the examinations. Ning had long expected to reach the chief ministership; on the day he passed, his name was thirteenth. Reading Zhi's essay he admired it all the more and placed him in the thirteenth rank. In the examination hall they called this "passing the robe and bowl," as in Chan transmission.

units.zh: 後質果繼凝登相位。）〉
units.en: Later Zhi indeed succeeded Ning as chief minister.〉
units.literal: Later Zhi indeed succeeded Ning in the chief ministership.〉

units.zh: 明宗益加器重，遷中書舍人、工部侍郎，皆充學士。
units.en: Mingzong valued him more, making him secretariat drafter and vice minister of works while retaining his Hanlin post.
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong valued him all the more, promoting him to Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Works, both while serving as academician.

units.zh: 晉有天下，拜端明殿學士，兼判度支，轉戶部侍郎，會廢端明之職，復入翰林充承旨。
units.en: When Jin held the realm he became academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and oversaw revenue, then vice minister of revenue. When that academy was abolished he returned to the Hanlin as chief drafter.
units.literal: When Jin held the realm he was made Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance, concurrently overseeing the Revenue Bureau, then Vice Minister of Revenue; when the Brilliant Governance post was abolished he re-entered the Hanlin as Chief Drafter.

units.zh: 晉祖每召問以時事，言皆稱旨。
units.en: The Jin founder summoned him on affairs of state; his answers always pleased.
units.literal: The Jin Ancestor whenever summoned him to ask about current affairs found his words all to the purpose.

units.zh: 五年，拜中書侍郎平章事。
units.en: In the fifth year he became vice minister of the Secretariat and grand councilor.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 六年秋，晉高祖將幸鄴都，時襄州安從進反狀已彰，凝乃奏曰：「車駕離闕，安從進或有悖逆，何以待之？」
units.en: In autumn of the sixth year Gaozu of Jin was bound for Yedu while An Congjin of Xiang showed open rebellion. Ning memorialized: "If the throne leaves the capital, Congjin may rebel—what is our plan?"
units.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year Emperor Gaozu of Jin was about to visit Yedu; at that time An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture's rebellious intent was already clear, and Ning memorialized: "If the imperial carriage leaves the capital, An Congjin may turn disloyal—how shall we meet it?"

units.zh: 晉高祖曰：「卿意如何？」
units.en: Gaozu asked, "What do you advise?"
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "What is your view?"

units.zh: 凝曰：「以臣料之，先人有奪人之心，臨事即不及也。
units.en: Ning said, "By my estimate, one must seize the initiative before the other does; when the crisis arrives it is already too late.
units.literal: Ning said, "By my estimate, men who seize others' possessions beforehand lack resolve when events come; they fall short.

units.zh: 欲預出宣敕十數道，密付開封尹鄭王，令有緩急即旋填將校姓名，令領兵擊之。」
units.en: Prepare a dozen blank edicts in secret for the Prince of Zheng as Kaifeng prefect: in crisis he can fill in commanders' names and send troops at once."
units.literal: I wish to prepare a dozen or so edicts in advance and secretly entrust them to the Prince of Zheng as Prefect of Kaifeng, so that in urgency he may at once fill in officers' names and order them to lead troops to strike."

units.zh: 晉高祖從之。
units.en: Gaozu agreed.
units.literal: Emperor Gaozu followed this.

units.zh: 及聞唐、鄧奏報，鄭王如所敕，遣騎將李建崇、監軍焦繼勛等領兵討焉，相遇於湖陽，從進出於不意，甚訝其神速，以至於敗，由凝之力也。
units.en: When Tang and Deng reported, the Prince of Zheng did as ordered, sending Li Jianchong, Jiao Jixun, and others. They met Congjin at Huyang; caught off guard by their speed, he was defeated—Ning's doing.
units.literal: When reports came from Tang and Deng, the Prince of Zheng acted as commanded, sending Cavalry General Li Jianchong, Military Commissioner Jiao Jixun, and others to lead troops against him. They met at Huyang; Congjin, taken unawares, was greatly astonished at their speed and was defeated—through Ning's power.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，加右僕射。
units.en: When the Young Emperor succeeded he was made right vice director.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he was made Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 開運初，罷相守本官，未幾，轉左僕射。
units.en: Early in Kaiyun he left the chief ministership but kept his post; soon he became left vice director.
units.literal: Early in Kaiyun he was dismissed from the chief ministership and kept his original office; before long he was changed to Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 漢興，授太子太保。
units.en: When Han arose he was made grand guardian of the heir.
units.literal: When Han arose he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 國初，遷太子太傅。
units.en: At the state's founding he became grand tutor of the heir.
units.literal: At the founding of the state he was moved to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 顯德二年秋，以背疽卒於其第，年五十八。
units.en: In autumn, Xiande year two, he died of a back carbuncle at home, aged fifty-eight.
units.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Xiande he died of a back carbuncle at his residence, aged fifty-eight.

units.zh: 輟視朝兩日，詔贈侍中。
units.en: Audience was suspended two days; he was posthumously made palace attendant.
units.literal: Court audience was suspended two days; an edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 凝性好修整，自釋褐至登臺輔。
units.en: Ning loved polish from his first office to the chief ministership:
units.literal: Ning's nature loved order and polish; from first leaving the russet robe to reaching the chief ministership,

units.zh: 車服仆從，必加華楚，進退容止偉如也。
units.en: carriages, dress, and attendants he kept splendid; in movement and stillness his bearing was imposing.
units.literal: carriages, dress, and attendants he always made splendid; in advancing and withdrawing his bearing and manner were imposing.

units.zh: 又好延納後進，士無賢不肖，皆虛懷以待之，或致其仕進，故甚有當時之譽。
units.en: He welcomed juniors, worthy or not, with open mind, and often advanced them—hence his great repute.
units.literal: He also loved to receive and advance the younger generation; whether a scholar was worthy or not, he met all with open mind, and sometimes secured their advancement—hence he had great repute in his day.

units.zh: 平生為文章，長於短歌艷曲，尤好聲譽。
units.en: He wrote all his life, excelling in short lyrics, and especially courted fame.
units.literal: In life he wrote, excelling in short songs and passionate lyrics, and especially loved reputation.

units.zh: 有集百卷，自篆於版，模印數百帙，分惠於人焉。
units.en: He compiled a hundred scrolls, carved the blocks himself, printed hundreds of copies, and gave them away.
units.literal: He had a collection of a hundred scrolls, carved the blocks himself, printed several hundred fascicles, and distributed them as gifts.

units.zh: 〈（《宋朝類苑》：和魯公凝有艷詞一編名《香奩集》，凝後貴，乃嫁其名為韓偓，今世傳韓偓《香奩集》，乃凝所為也。
units.en: 〈Classified Anecdotes of the Song Dynasty〉: He Duke of Lu Ning wrote passionate lyrics called Collection of the Perfumed Toilet. After he rose high he attributed them to Han Wo; the Han Wo collection transmitted today is Ning's.
units.literal: 〈Classified Anecdotes of the Song Dynasty〉: He Duke of Lu Ning had a volume of passionate lyrics called Collection of the Perfumed Toilet. After Ning rose high he married off the name to Han Wo; the Han Wo Collection of the Perfumed Toilet transmitted in the world today is in fact Ning's work.

units.zh: 凝生平著述，分為《演綸》、遊藝、孝悌、《疑獄》、《香奩》、《籯金》六集，自為《遊藝集序》云：「予有《香奩》、《籯金》二集，不行於世。」
units.en: His works fell into six collections: Evolution of the Silken Canon, Recreations, Filial Piety, Doubtful Cases, Perfumed Toilet, and Casket of Gold. In his Preface to Recreations he wrote: "My Perfumed Toilet and Casket of Gold do not circulate."
units.literal: Ning's writings in life were divided into six collections: Evolution of the Silken Canon, Recreations, Filial Piety and Fraternal Duty, Doubtful Cases, Perfumed Toilet, and Casket of Gold. In his own Preface to Recreations he said: "I have the Perfumed Toilet and Casket of Gold collections, which do not circulate in the world."

units.zh: 凝在政府避議論，諱其名，又欲後人知，故於《遊藝集序》實之，此凝之意也。）〉
units.en: In office he avoided debate and hid the name yet wished posterity to know, so he stated it in the Preface to Recreations—that was his intent.〉
units.literal: In government Ning avoided debate, concealed the name, yet wished later men to know; therefore in the Preface to Recreations he stated it plainly—this was Ning's intent.〉

units.zh: 長子峻，卒於省郎。
units.en: His eldest son Jun died as a provincial bureau officer.
units.literal: The eldest son Jun died as a provincial bureau officer.

units.zh: 次子峴，
units.en: The second son Xian,
units.literal: The second son Xian,

units.zh: 〈（《綿繡萬花谷》：範蜀公《蒙求》云：和峴，晉相和凝之子。
units.en: 〈Brocade and Myriad Flowers〉: Fan the Duke of Shu's Seeking the Obscure says He Xian was son of Jin chancellor He Ning.
units.literal: 〈Brocade and Myriad Flowers〉: Fan the Duke of Shu in Seeking the Obscure says: He Xian was son of Jin chancellor He Ning.

units.zh: 峴生，會凝入翰林、加金紫、知貢舉，凝喜曰：「我生平美事，三者並集，此子宜於我矣。」
units.en: At Xian's birth Ning entered the Hanlin, received gold-purple, and oversaw examinations. He rejoiced: "Three fine things of my life together—this child suits me."
units.literal: When Xian was born, it happened that Ning entered the Hanlin, received gold-purple, and oversaw examinations. Ning rejoiced and said, "The fine things of my life—three together at once—this child suits me."

units.zh: 因名曰三美。）〉
units.en: He named him Sanmei, Three Beauties.〉
units.literal: He therefore named him Sanmei [Three Beauties].〉

units.zh: 仕皇朝為司勛員外郎。
units.en: He served the court as vice director in the Bureau of Merit.
units.literal: He served the imperial court as Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit.

units.zh: 蘇禹珪，字元錫，其先出於武功，近世家高密，今為郡人也。
units.en: Su Yugui, courtesy name Yuansi, traced descent to Wugong; his line had lately settled in Gaomi and were now men of the prefecture.
units.literal: Su Yugui, styled Yuansi, was descended from Wugong; his family had lately settled in Gaomi and now were natives of the prefecture.

units.zh: 父仲容，以儒學稱於鄉里，唐末舉《九經》，補廣文助教，遷輔唐令，累贈太師。
units.en: Father Zhongrong was famed locally for scholarship. Late in Tang he passed the Nine Classics, became Broad Learning assistant, rose to magistrate of Futang, and was repeatedly enfeoffed grand preceptor.
units.literal: His father Zhongrong was famed in the district for classical learning; late in Tang he passed the Nine Classics, was made assistant in the Broad Learning college, rose to magistrate of Futang, and was repeatedly enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 禹珪性謙和，虛襟接物，克構父業，以五經中第，辟遼州倅職，歷青、鄆從事，轉潞、並管記，累檢校官至戶部郎中。
units.en: Yugui was modest and open, built on his father's learning, passed the Five Classics, served as aide in Liaozhou and staff in Qing and Yan, became recorder in Lu and Bing, and rose by inspection to revenue bureau director.
units.literal: Yugui was modest and gentle, received others with open breast, built on his father's work, passed the Five Classics, was recruited as aide in Liaozhou, served as staff officer in Qing and Yan, became recorder in Lu and Bing, and by cumulative inspection reached Bureau Director in Revenue.

units.zh: 漢高祖作鎮並門，奏為兼判。
units.en: When Han Gaozu governed Bing Gate he had Yugui made concurrent overseer.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu held Bing Gate as military governor he memorialized for Yugui as concurrent overseer.

units.zh: 開運末，契丹入汴，漢祖即位於晉陽，授中書侍郎平章事。
units.en: At Kaiyun's end the Khitans entered Bian. Han Gaozu took the throne at Jinyang and made Yugui vice minister and grand councilor.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitans entered Bian; Han Ancestor took the throne at Jinyang and appointed Yugui Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 漢祖輗阼，兼刑部尚書，俄加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。
units.en: On Han's accession he also became minister of punishments, then right vice director and grand academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.
units.literal: When Han Ancestor succeeded he was also Minister of Punishments; soon he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Gathering Worthies.

units.zh: 漢祖大漸，與蘇逢吉、楊邠等受顧命，立少主。
units.en: When Han fell gravely ill, he with Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and others received the deathbed charge and installed the young emperor.
units.literal: When Han Ancestor fell gravely ill, together with Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and others he received the final charge and established the young ruler.

units.zh: 明年，轉左僕射。
units.en: The next year he became left vice director.
units.literal: The next year he was made Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 三年冬，太祖入平內難，禹珪遁入都城，為兵士所擄。
units.en: In winter of year three Taizu entered to quell strife. Yugui fled into the capital and was seized by troops.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year Taizu entered to quell internal strife; Yugui fled into the capital and was seized by soldiers.

units.zh: 翌日，太祖令人求之，既見，撫慰甚至，尋復其位。
units.en: Next day Taizu sent for him, comforted him deeply, and soon restored his post.
units.literal: The next day Taizu sent men to seek him; when seen he was comforted to the utmost and soon restored to office.

units.zh: 國初，加守司空，尋罷相守本官。
units.en: At the founding he was made acting grand master of works; soon he left the chief ministership but kept his post.
units.literal: At the founding he was made acting Grand Master of Works; soon dismissed from the chief ministership and kept his original office.

units.zh: 世宗嗣位，封莒國公，未幾，受代歸第。
units.en: When Shizong succeeded he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju; soon he retired home.
units.literal: When Shizong succeeded he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju; before long he yielded office and returned home.

units.zh: 顯德三年正月旦，與客對食之際，暴疾而卒，時年六十二。
units.en: On New Year's Day, Xiande year three, dining with guests, he suddenly fell ill and died at sixty-two.
units.literal: On the first day of the first month of the third year of Xiande, while dining with guests, he suddenly fell ill and died, aged sixty-two.

units.zh: 禹珪純厚長者，遭遇漢祖，及蘇逢吉夷滅，禹珪恬然無咎，時人以為積善之報也。
units.en: A pure, generous elder, he served Han Gaozu; when Su Fengji was destroyed he remained unscathed—men called it reward for virtue.
units.literal: Yugui was a pure, generous elder; he met Han Ancestor's favor, and when Su Fengji was exterminated Yugui remained untroubled—men of the time took it as reward for accumulated goodness.

units.zh: 子德祥，登進士第，累歷臺省。
units.en: Son Dexiang passed the Jinshi and served in the censorate and secretariat.
units.literal: His son Dexiang passed the Jinshi and rose through the censorate and secretariat.

units.zh: 景範，淄州長山人。
units.en: Jing Fan was from Changshan in Zizhou.
units.literal: Jing Fan was a native of Changshan in Zizhou.

units.zh: 〈（案：此下有闕文。
units.en: 〈Note: Text is missing below.
units.literal: 〈Note: Text is missing below.

units.zh: 據《世宗紀》，景範父名初，以戶部郎中致仕。）〉
units.en: According to Shizong's annals, Fan's father was named Chu and retired as revenue bureau director.〉
units.literal: According to the Basic Annals of Shizong, Fan's father's given name was Chu; he retired as Bureau Director in Revenue.〉

units.zh: 世宗之北征也，命為東京副留守。
units.en: On Shizong's northern campaign he was made vice guardian of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: On Shizong's northern campaign Fan was ordered Vice Guardian of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 車駕回自河東，世宗以艱於國用，乃以範為中書侍郎平章事、判三司。
units.en: Returning from Hedong, Shizong, pressed for revenue, made Fan vice minister, grand councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Hedong, Shizong, finding state revenue strained, made Fan Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》載：世宗即位，七月癸巳，制曰：「朕自履宸極，思平泰階，出一令慮下民之未從，行一事懼上穹之罔祐，晨興夕惕，終歲於茲。
units.en: 〈The Imperial Tortoise Mirror records: On Shizong's accession, guisi of the seventh month, an edict said: "Since I took the throne I have sought to level the great stair. One order I fear the people have not followed; one act I fear Heaven has not blessed—diligent dawn to dusk the whole year through.
units.literal: 〈The Imperial Tortoise Mirror records: When Shizong took the throne, on the day guisi of the seventh month an edict said: "Since I assumed the august pinnacle I have thought to level the great stair; issuing one order I fear the people have not yet followed, doing one thing I fear Heaven has not yet blessed it—rising early and resting late, the whole year thus.

units.zh: 雖禮讓漸聞興行，而風雨未之咸若，豈刑政之所闕，而德教之未孚哉！
units.en: Though courtesy is heard to rise, wind and rain are not yet harmonious—is government at fault, or teaching not yet trusted?
units.literal: Though ritual yielding is gradually heard to arise, wind and rain have not all been harmonious—can it be that punishments and government are lacking, or that virtue and teaching have not won trust?

units.zh: 由是進用良臣，輔宣皇化，雖朕志先定，亦輿情具瞻，爰擇佳辰，誕敷明命。
units.en: Therefore I advance good ministers to proclaim the royal way; though my will was first, public sentiment also watches—I choose an auspicious day and proclaim a bright mandate.
units.literal: Therefore I advance good ministers to assist and proclaim imperial transformation; though my will was set first, public sentiment also looks on all sides—choosing an auspicious day I proclaim a bright mandate.

units.zh: 樞密院直學士、中大夫、尚書工部侍郎、上柱國、晉陽縣開國男、食邑三百戶、賜紫金魚袋範，昔佐先帝，每罄嘉謨，逮事眇躬，愈傾忠節，奉上得大臣之體，檢身為君子之儒。
units.en: Fan, Direct Academician of the Privy Council, Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Minister of Works, Supreme Pillar of the State, Baron of Jinyang with three hundred households, bearer of the gold-purple fish tally—formerly aided the late emperor with every counsel fully offered; serving my slight person, his loyal resolve bends all the more; in serving his superiors he attains a great minister's form, in examining himself he is a gentleman's scholar.
units.literal: Fan, Direct Academician of the Privy Council, Grand Master of the Palace, Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works, Supreme Pillar of the State, Baron of Jinyang with three hundred households' fief, bearer of the gold-purple fish tally—formerly aided the late emperor, every counsel fully offered; serving my slight person, his loyal resolve bends all the more; in serving the above he attains a great minister's form, in examining himself he is a gentleman's scholar.

units.zh: 一昨戎輅親征，皇都是守，贊勛賢於留府，副征發於行營，軍政所需，國用無闕。
units.en: When lately the emperor campaigned in person while the capital was guarded, he praised worthies at the rear capital office and assisted levies at the camp—military needs were met and revenue did not fail.
units.literal: When lately the war carriage campaigned in person and the imperial capital was guarded, he praised the worthy at the rear capital office and assisted levy and dispatch at the campaign camp—military needs were met and state revenue unlacking.

units.zh: 今則靈臺偃革，宣室圖功，思先朝欲用之言，成聖考得賢之美，俾參大政，仍掌利權。
units.en: Now arms rest and merit is plotted; remembering the former court's wish to employ him, fulfilling the sage's gain of worth—let him share great government and hold fiscal power.
units.literal: Now the Spirit Tower rests arms and the Hall of Proclamation plots merit; thinking of the former court's wish to employ him, fulfilling the sage's gain of the worthy—let him share great government and still hold fiscal power.

units.zh: 爾其明聽朕言，往敷洪化，予欲則垂象而清品匯，爾則順天道以序彜倫，余欲恤刑名而息戰爭，爾則謹憲章而恢廟略。
units.en: Hear my words and spread great transformation: when I wish, signs clear all ranks; you follow Heaven's way and order relations; when I ease punishments and still war, you keep statutes and restore strategy.
units.literal: Clearly hear my words and go to spread great transformation: when I wish, the heavens show signs and all ranks grow clear; you shall follow Heaven's way and order human relations; when I wish to ease punishments and still war, you shall keep statutes and restore temple strategy.

units.zh: 天人之際懸合，軍民之事罔渝，則國相之尊，非爾孰處，邦計之重，惟材是臧。
units.en: When Heaven and man align and army and people hold firm, who but you for chief minister? For state accounts, only talent avails.
units.literal: When Heaven and man hang together and army and people do not stray, then the state's chief minister—who but you? The state's accounts—only talent is stored.

units.zh: 勉思倜儻以致君，勿效因循而保位，佇聞成績，用副虛懷。
units.en: Strive boldly to serve the ruler; do not cling to routine and office—await achievement to match my hopes.
units.literal: Strive with bold resolve to serve the ruler; do not imitate routine and cling to place—await achievement to match my open mind.

units.zh: 可正議大夫、中書侍郎平章事，判三司。」）〉
units.en: Appointed grand master of court discussion, vice minister, grand councilor, overseer of the Three Bureaus."〉
units.literal: May be Grand Master of Court Discussion, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and overseer of the Three Bureaus."〉

units.zh: 範為人厚重剛正，無所屈撓，然理繁治劇，非其所長，雖悉心盡瘁，終無稱職之譽。
units.en: Fan was weighty and upright, yielding to none; yet complexity was not his strength—though he wore himself out, he won no praise for competence.
units.literal: Fan as a man was weighty, upright, and bowed to nothing; yet governing complexity and urgency was not his strength—though he gave his heart and wore himself out, in the end he won no praise for competence.

units.zh: 世宗知之，因其有疾，乃罷司計。
units.en: Shizong knew it; when illness came he removed him from fiscal office.
units.literal: Shizong knew this; because he was ill he dismissed him from fiscal office.

units.zh: 尋以父喪罷相東歸。
units.en: Soon his father's mourning took him from office eastward.
units.literal: Soon on his father's mourning he left the chief ministership and returned east.

units.zh: 顯德三年冬，以疾卒於鄉里。
units.en: In winter, Xiande year three, he died of illness at home.
units.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande he died of illness in his home district.

units.zh: 優詔贈侍中，官為立碑焉。
units.en: A gracious edict made him palace attendant posthumously, and the office raised a stele.
units.literal: A gracious edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant, and the office erected a stele for him.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫以稽古之力，取秉鈞之位者，豈常人乎！
units.en: The historiographer says: To reach the chief ministership by power of antiquarian learning—is that a common man?
units.literal: The historiographer says: To take the position of holding the scales by power of examining antiquity—is that a common man?

units.zh: 然文紀耽於貨殖，裔孫傷於齷齪，則知全其德者鮮矣。
units.en: Yet Wenji clung to profit and Yisun to pettiness—few kept virtue whole.
units.literal: Yet Wenji was addicted to trade, Yisun wounded by pettiness—then one knows those who kept their virtue whole were few.

units.zh: 如成績之文采，元錫之履行，景範之純厚，皆得謂之君子儒矣。
units.en: Chengzhi's literary grace, Yuansi's conduct, Fan's pure weight—all were gentleman's scholars.
units.literal: As for Chengzhi's literary color, Yuansi's conduct, and Fan's pure weight—all may be called gentleman's scholars.

units.zh: 以之爰立，何用不臧。
units.en: With such men in high office, what need would go unmet?
units.literal: With such men established in office, what use would not be fulfilled?

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.action: Replace the reign-wide life interval and hint with the accession’s sourced point chronology, preserving the succession fact.

findings.action: Remove or recast the false closed life intervals and derived hints; retain the office-history fact without inventing an endpoint.

findings.action: Remove the false life chronology and active hints; retain the allusions as retrospective references.

findings.action: Remove the false 940–955 life intervals and hints and retain/reclassify the source facts as posthumous reception.

findings.problem: A sequence after the Huliupei battle was collapsed into the battle’s AD 923 point date.
findings.action: Use a one-sided post-923 bound if retained, or remove the date and hint; do not invent a point year.

findings.action: Remove the false life chronology and hint and retain the evidence as a retrospective attribution/reference.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported period and active hint while retaining the undated death-in-office fact.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported interval and hint while retaining the bibliographical quotation as an undated/reception fact.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported date and hint from the son’s career statement; preserve the undated career fact.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported reign interval and hint while retaining the undated father-name and retirement source fact.
